title: Finite affine monomial models for a graded sheaf module
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $\mathcal B=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal B_d$ be a commutative graded $\mathcal O_S$-algebra and $L=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}L_d$ a graded $\mathcal B$-module [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], with all homogeneous pieces quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Suppose $\mathcal B_0=\mathcal O_S$, $\mathcal B_1$ is coherent and generates $\mathcal B$, and $L$ is locally generated by finitely many homogeneous sections, in arbitrary nonnegative degrees [def-sfb-graded-sheaf-generation]. There is a finite affine open cover $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ of $S$, with $A_i$ Noetherian, and finite lists $x_{i,1},\ldots,x_{i,r_i}\in\mathcal B_1(U_i)$ and $e_{i,1},\ldots,e_{i,t_i}$ with $e_{i,j}\in L_{b_{i,j}}(U_i)$, such that for every $d\geq0$ the restrictions of $x_i^\alpha$ with $|\alpha|=d$ generate $\mathcal B_d|_{U_i}$ as a sheaf, and the restrictions of $x_i^\alpha e_{i,j}$ with $|\alpha|+b_{i,j}=d$ generate $L_d|_{U_i}$ as a sheaf [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. The same finite lists generate the respective modules of sections over $U_i$. Thus $C_i=\bigoplus_d\mathcal B_d(U_i)$ is an $A_i$-algebra generated by the $x_{i,k}$ and $M_i=\bigoplus_d L_d(U_i)$ is a $C_i$-module generated by the $e_{i,j}$, and each $(M_i)_d$ is a finite $A_i$-module (finite means finitely generated). For every $s\in U_i$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p\subset A_i$ there is a $\kappa(s)$-linear isomorphism
$$L_{d,s}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\kappa(s)\ \cong\ (M_i)_d\otimes_{A_i}\kappa(\mathfrak p),$$
using the canonical residue-field identification [def-weil-residue-field] and the actual module stalk [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. Empty covers and empty generating lists are allowed.

proof.text: For each point $s$, choose a neighbourhood $W_s$ and finitely many homogeneous module generators $e_{s,j}$ of degrees $b_{s,j}$ using [def-sfb-graded-sheaf-generation]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] choose an affine neighbourhood $s\in U_s\subseteq W_s$ and restrict these sections. The defining local spanning condition persists: every open inside $U_s$ is also inside $W_s$. Quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] selects finitely many $U_s$ covering $S$; write them $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. Each $A_i$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. If $S$ is empty, select the empty cover.

source.place: Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens; quasi-compactness selects a finite subcover; generation hypothesis as in the item

proof.text: Coherence of $\mathcal B_1$ includes finite type by [pqf-def-coherent]; restriction preserves this condition by restricting each local finite free surjection. Quasi-coherence of $\mathcal B_1$ is a hypothesis, and $\mathcal B_1|_{U_i}$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] (2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-finite-type-generating-sections] on each $U_i$ to choose finitely many sections $x_{i,k}\in\mathcal B_1(U_i)$ generating $\mathcal B_1|_{U_i}$ as a sheaf. Fix one $i$ for the remaining argument and suppress its index. The homogeneous module sections from step 1 and these degree-one algebra sections are now defined on the same affine open.

proof.text:
Induct on $d$ to prove that every section of $\mathcal B_d$ on an open $V\subseteq U$ is, near each point of $V$, an $\mathcal O$-linear combination of restrictions of the $x^\alpha$ with $|\alpha|=d$. For $d=0$, the structural identification $\mathcal B_0=\mathcal O_S$ gives the single monomial $x^0=1$. For $d+1$, degree-one generation [def-sfb-graded-sheaf-generation] expresses a section locally as a finite sum $\sum_
u c_
u a_
u b_
u$, with $a_
u$ of degree one and $b_
u$ of degree $d$. Expand each $a_
u$ locally in the fixed $x_k$ using step 2 and the local-lift form of sheaf generation [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], and each $b_
u$ locally in degree-$d$ monomials by induction. For a fixed point intersect the finitely many resulting neighbourhoods; this is an open neighbourhood, with no assertion of affineness. Bilinearity, associativity and commutativity [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures] turn the product into a sum of terms $c x_kx^\alpha=c x^{\alpha+\epsilon_k}$. These have degree $d+1$, proving the induction for every open $V$.

source.place: Tag 00K0, lemma-graded-module-fg, monomial expansion adapted to the local spanning definition

proof.text: For a section $y\in L_d(V)$ and a point of $V\subseteq U$, local homogeneous generation [def-sfb-graded-sheaf-generation] expresses $y$ near that point as a finite $\mathcal O$-linear sum of $a_j e_j$ with $b_j\leq d$ and $a_j\in\mathcal B_{d-b_j}$. Apply step 3 to each of the finitely many coefficients and intersect the resulting neighbourhoods. Bilinearity of the graded action [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures] gives a local linear expression in $x^\alpha e_j$ with $|\alpha|+b_j=d$. Both degree-$d$ lists are finite: each coordinate of $\alpha\in\mathbb N^r$ with $|\alpha|\leq d$ lies in $\{0,\ldots,d\}$, and the list of $j$ is finite. When $b_j>d$ there is no such term. For $r=0$ there is exactly one exponent vector, of degree zero; for an empty module-generator list the local expression is zero. Thus these statements include all zero and empty cases.

source.place: Tag 00K0, lemma-graded-module-fg, finite monomials of the prescribed degree

proof.text: For either of the finite degree-$d$ lists just obtained, let $F$ denote its target sheaf ($\mathcal B_d|_U$ or $L_d|_U$), and form the map $\varphi:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus N}\to F$ sending the basis to that list. Its source is quasi-coherent with sections $A^N$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module], and its target is quasi-coherent on $U$ by hypothesis and [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] (2). The local expressions in steps 3--4 say exactly that $\operatorname{Im}\varphi=F$, using the local-image definition in [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image]. Part (3) of that node gives $F(U)=\varphi_U(A^N)$, so the SAME list generates the module of affine sections. In particular each $L_d(U)$ is finite over $A$. The products and actions on sections satisfy the graded laws by [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. Every element of the algebraic direct sums $C=\bigoplus_d\mathcal B_d(U)$ and $M=\bigoplus_dL_d(U)$ has only finitely many homogeneous components. Applying the degreewise section expressions to those components shows that the $x_k$ generate $C$ as an $A$-algebra and the $e_j$ generate $M$ as a $C$-module. No interchange of global sections with a sheaf direct sum is asserted or needed.

proof.text:
Fix $s\in U$ with prime $\mathfrak p$, and put $N=L_d(U)$, $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ and $k=\kappa(s)$. By [lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization], $N\to L_{d,s}$ is localization at $A\setminus\mathfrak p$, through the actual germ map. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ compatibly with ring germs; [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] identifies $k$ with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ compatibly with $A\to k$. Write a localized module element as $m/t$, with $t\notin\mathfrak p$. Define
$$\Phi:(L_{d,s}\otimes_R k)\longrightarrow N\otimes_A k,\qquad (m/t)\otimes c\longmapsto m\otimes\bar t^{-1}c.$$
This is well defined: equality of fractions becomes equality after multiplication by some $u\notin\mathfrak p$, whose image in $k$ is invertible. It is balanced over $R$, since moving $a/v\in A_{\mathfrak p}$ to the second tensor factor multiplies it by $\bar a/\bar v$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] therefore gives a $k$-linear map. Its inverse is $m\otimes c\mapsto(m/1)\otimes c$, which is $A$-balanced. The two composites on pure tensors are the identity, using $(m/t)\otimes c=(m/1)\otimes\bar t^{-1}c$ in the first tensor product; pure tensors generate. This is the required isomorphism, with $N=(M_i)_d$.
